newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - Don't write off Hurricanes yet - Hewitt.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Don't write off Hurricanes yet - Hewitt.

text.p: WELLINGTON, May 19 - When the Wellington Hurricanes walked from their Athletic Park dressing room last night it was, said hooker Norman Hewitt, the start of a new week.
Hewitt, outstanding in the 35-29 defeat by the ACT Brumbies, says the Hurricanes' season is not over.
The team now face one of the really hard tasks of Super 12 rugby -- having to win the semifinal in Canberra to make the final.
"We still have to be positive. It isn't over. We have a semi over there, and I know the players won't put their heads down and say we're just happy to be here in this semi position'.
"We'll pick ourselves up out of this as long as we all know that we have to learn. And we have to learn very quickly on the things we have to improve on."
Hewitt remarked on the absolute silence in the dressing room yesterday.

"We are hurting because there are so many things we let ourselves down with -- the expectations of the game, the amount of people that came to watch, and the fact we weren't able to produce the style of rugby we've produced over the last five or six games.

"So it was really frustrating. What we talked about during the week about defence and what we were going to do to turn that into attack we just didn't do. David Knox and George Gregan showed that if you don't shut them down, they're going to score points. But we can't dwell on this too long."
Hewitt never felt the Hurricanes were without a chance of winning, even as time ticked away.

"Even at that last scrum we asked Colin Hawke how much time we had. He said just under a minute and Bull (captain Mark Allen) said it didn't matter because we should score from there. And I thought we would as well. But we didn't, and that was the
game.
"We have to start being really positive, because it's not over. We leave on Tuesday and there's a game to be won. We have to say that we can improve a good deal on today."
All Black coach John Hart agreed with Hewitt that the tables could be turned in Canberra next Saturday.

"ACT deserved to win. They played a bit better. But I've just told the team that they can be very proud of where they are and that while they've lost they are still in the semifinal and that they've got a big chance," Hart said yesterday.
"I think they have the ability to win away -- they are one of the sides that has got ability to win away. We've got a really special team here.
"I think they might even have an advantage in playing away because the other guys will be up in the air now. They'll think they are invincible at home, because they've won a lot of games there.
"These guys (the Hurricanes) just have to set for it."
Hart said efforts by Hurricanes players through the season promoted team individuals into trial team contention.

Hart will name his two All Black trial teams tomorrow and Hurricanes players Christian Cullen, Tana Umaga, Mark Cooksley, Norman Hewitt and Mark Allen should all make sides, with Jason O'Halloran being on the fringe.
Hart said injured Alama Ieremia would not be considered for the trial.
"We want him to work his way back slowly and be careful about it. I believe he's had a special kind of season so far."
